Module 08: Primer & Probe RAA Design

Isothermal amplification technologies, such as Recombinase Aid Amplification (RAA) and Recombinase Polymerase Amplification (RPA), are vital for point-of-care (POC) molecular diagnostics. Unlike thermal cycling PCR, RAA operates at a constant low temperature (\(37^\circ\text{C}\) to \(42^\circ\text{C}\)).

Module 08 integrates PrimerLab-Genomic, an in-house tool developed by the CORE-Lab Research group (GitHub Repository). PrimerLab-Genomic utilizes the core engine of Primer3 (Koressaar and Remm 2007; Untergasser et al. 2012) for candidate search and incorporates the ViennaRNA (Lorenz et al. 2011) package to evaluate complex secondary structures under isothermal, high-magnesium conditions.

1. Biophysical and Thermodynamic Rules for RAA Design

RAA reaction dynamics differ fundamentally from traditional PCR. Because the double-stranded DNA template is unwound by a recombinase-primer complex rather than heat denaturation, the primers must satisfy strict biophysical criteria:

                       ◄─── 30 to 35 bp Forward Primer ───►
5'- ... NNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNN ... -3'
        ||||||||||||||||||||||||||||||||||||||||||||||||||||||
3'- ... NNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNN ... -5'
                                            ▲
                     [Critical 3' End: 100% Conserved (No IUPAC)]

1.1. Primer and Probe Dimensions

  • Primer Length: RAA primers must be 30 to 35 nucleotides long (compared to 18–22 bp for PCR). Shorter primers cannot form a stable recombinase filament and fail to initiate strand exchange at \(37^\circ\text{C}\).
  • Amplicon Length: The ideal product size range is 100 to 300 base pairs (maximum 500 bp) to ensure rapid amplification within 15–20 minutes under isothermal conditions.
  • Exo-Probe Structure: Fluorescent RAA exo-probes must be 46 to 52 nucleotides long. The probe sequence is modified internally:
    • An abasic site analog, Tetrahydrofuran (THF / dSpacer), is placed in the middle (at least 30 bp from the 5’ end and 15 bp from the 3’ end).
    • A Fluorophore (e.g., FAM) and a Quencher (e.g., BHQ-1) are attached immediately adjacent to the THF site.
    • A 3’ blocking group (e.g., phosphate or C3 spacer) prevents the probe from acting as a primer. During hybridization, the enzyme Exonuclease III cleaves the THF site, separating the fluorophore from the quencher to generate a fluorescent signal.

1.2. Temperature & Salt Corrections

Isothermal assay dynamics require distinct salt formulations (typically \(14\text{ mM}\) Magnesium acetate \([Mg^{2+}]\) and \(50\text{ mM}\) monovalent cations \([K^+]\)).

To ensure accurate melting temperature (\(T_m\)) prediction, PrimerLab-Genomic integrates thermodynamic parameters with salt-correction corrections (Lorenz et al. 2011) adjusted to these high-magnesium conditions. Standard PCR formulas underestimate the stabilizing effect of \(14\text{ mM}\) \(Mg^{2+}\), which raises the effective \(T_m\) of long primers.

2. Evolutionary Exclusion Check

To prevent diagnostic escape (false negatives caused by ongoing viral evolution), the Snakemake rule m08_generate_payload programmatically extracts high-entropy positions and positive selection sites (identified by MEME/ASR in Modules 05 & 06) and converts them into Exclusion Blocks:

  • 3’ End Protection: Primers are strictly forbidden from having any mutations or degenerate bases within the last 5 to 8 nucleotides of their 3’ end. Mismatches at the 3’ terminal block prevent DNA polymerase extension, causing assay failure.
  • Probe Body Protection: Probes are restricted from containing high-entropy coordinates to maintain binding stability.

3. Degenerate Rescue System

In highly variable viral genomes, finding a 100% conserved 30–35 bp target is frequently impossible. Module 08 resolves this through the Degenerate Rescue Engine (scripts/m08_degenerate_rescue.py):

  1. IUPAC Incorporation: If a position within a candidate primer has a Minor Allele Frequency (MAF) above the threshold (default: \(0.10\)), the engine “rescues” the candidate by introducing a degenerate IUPAC base (e.g., \(R\) for \(A/G\), \(Y\) for \(C/T\)).
  2. Complexity Constraint: To prevent signal dilution, the total degeneracy (calculated as the product of the degenerate base multiplicities) is capped at a maximum multiplier (default: \(16\), e.g., a primer with two 2-fold degenerate bases has a complexity of \(2 \times 2 = 4\)).
  3. Worst-Case Thermodynamic Evaluation: The engine invokes ViennaRNA (Lorenz et al. 2011) to model secondary structures (hairpins, homodimers, heterodimers) for every individual nucleotide combination represented by the degenerate primer. The thermodynamic score is determined by the worst-performing variant to ensure amplification stability across all target viral strains.

4. Configuration & Execution Commands (Tabset Examples)

Below are the configuration schemas, execution commands, and output data formats of Module 08:

  • 1. Configuration (config_influenza_a_mp.yaml)
  • 2. Payload Generation (YAML Config)
  • 3. PrimerLab Execution CLI
  • 4. Degenerate Rescue CLI
  • 5. Output: best_primers.json
# [M08] PrimerLab execution settings
primerlab:
  repo_path: "E:/Project/primerlab-genomic" # Path to local editable package
  template: "config/primerlab_templates/raa_exo_template.yaml"
  design:
    num_candidates: 100           # Number of primer-probe candidates to rank
    window_size: 150              # Sliding window for probe placement
    search_strategy: "exhaustive" # Search space mode
    hard_qc_filter: true          # Veto candidates failing GC or homopolymer checks
    degenerate:
      maf_threshold: 0.10         # Minimum MAF to trigger degenerate base rescue
      max_multiplier: 16          # Max degeneracy combination complexity limit
      thermo_eval_mode: "worst_case"
      vienna_temp: 37.0           # Reaction temperature (isothermal)
# Convert M07 manifest to PrimerLab payload config
python scripts/m08_payload_generator.py \
    --manifest results/influenza-a-mp-sea/m07/primer_targets_manifest.yaml \
    --template config/primerlab_templates/raa_exo_template.yaml \
    --outdir results/influenza-a-mp-sea/m08/degenerate \
    --mode degenerate \
    --num-candidates 100 \
    --window-size 150 \
    --search-strategy exhaustive \
    --hard-qc-filter True
# Execute PrimerLab isothermal RAA search
primerlab raa \
    --config results/influenza-a-mp-sea/m08/degenerate/primerlab_config_segment-MP.yaml \
    --out results/influenza-a-mp-sea/m08/degenerate \
    --validate
# Run Degenerate Rescue on candidate output files
python scripts/m08_degenerate_rescue.py \
    --manifest results/influenza-a-mp-sea/m07/primer_targets_manifest.yaml \
    --summary results/influenza-a-mp-sea/m08/degenerate/segment-MP/summary.json \
    --alternatives results/influenza-a-mp-sea/m08/degenerate/segment-MP/alternatives.json \
    --best-primers results/influenza-a-mp-sea/m08/degenerate/segment-MP/best_primers.json \
    --outdir results/influenza-a-mp-sea/m08/degenerate/segment-MP \
    --maf-threshold 0.10 \
    --max-multiplier 16 \
    --thermo-mode worst_case \
    --vienna-temp 37.0

4. Configuration & Parameterization

The assay design phase is controlled by the design parameters in config.yaml and the detailed thermodynamic template config/primerlab_template.yaml:

# [M08] Primer & Probe Design (PrimerLab)
design:
  min_primer_length: 30
  max_primer_length: 35
  min_probe_length: 46
  max_probe_length: 52
  max_degeneracy: 16

4.1. PrimerLab Thermodynamic Master Template (primerlab_template.yaml)

PrimerLab calculates DNA melting temperatures (\(T_m\)) using nearest-neighbor thermodynamic parameters and models secondary structures using ViennaRNA (Lorenz et al. 2011). Below are the key parameters defined in the template:

Parameter Path Allowed Values Default Value Purpose & Biological Meaning
parameters.thermodynamics.salt_monovalent Float \(\ge 0.0\) 50.0 Monovalent salt concentration (Na+ / K+ in mM). Used for salt-correction of DNA melting temperature.
parameters.thermodynamics.salt_divalent Float \(\ge 0.0\) 14.0 Divalent salt concentration (Mg2+ in mM). RAA specific. Isothermal amplification relies on high magnesium concentrations (~14 mM) to stabilize recombinase-DNA complexes.
parameters.thermodynamics.dntp_conc Float \(\ge 0.0\) 0.8 Concentration of dNTPs (mM). Higher than standard PCR to fuel fast isothermal transcription.
parameters.thermodynamics.dna_conc Float \(\ge 0.0\) 480.0 Total primer concentration (nM). RAA requires a highly crowded environment to drive recombinase-mediated strand invasion.
parameters.primer_size.opt Integer 32 Optimal length of RAA primers. Isothermal recombinase binding requires long primers (\(30-35\) bp) to successfully invade double-stranded DNA templates.
parameters.probe.type "exo", "taqman" "exo" The chemistry type. "exo" designs TwistAmp Exo-style probes (\(46-52\) bp) with an internal abasic site (THF spacer) for Endonuclease IV cleavage.
qc.vienna_ranking_limit Integer 50 The top 50 candidates from Primer3 are sent to ViennaRNA to calculate secondary structures (hairpins, homodimers, heterodimers) at the isothermal temperature of \(37^\circ\text{C}\).

4.2. How to Interpret PrimerLab Design Outputs

Module 08 outputs best_primers.json containing the physical profiles of the designed set:

  • Hairpin & Dimer \(\Delta G\): Represents the Gibbs free energy change of self-folding. Values closer to 0 (e.g. \(>-2.0\text{ kcal/mol}\)) are stable and safe. Values more negative than \(-5.0\text{ kcal/mol}\) indicate a high risk of primer-dimer formation, which will consume master-mix and cause false positives.
  • Degeneracy Multiplier: The number of unique primer sequences in the synthesized mix. A multiplier of 16 (e.g. 4 degenerate positions) means the active concentration of any single primer sequence is diluted to \(1/16\)-th. Keeping this below 16 ensures high diagnostic sensitivity.

5. Inputs, Outputs & Files

The files involved in Module 08 are summarized below:

File Role Path Format Description
Input Manifest results/{build}/m07/primer_targets_manifest.yaml YAML Targets and target sequences from Module 07.
Payload Config results/{build}/m08/{mode}/primerlab_config_{region}.yaml YAML Formatted input configuration for PrimerLab.
Best Primers results/{build}/m08/{mode}/{region}/best_primers.json JSON Ranked list of the top primer-probe candidate combinations.
Alternatives results/{build}/m08/{mode}/{region}/alternatives.json JSON Extended backup list of additional valid design candidates.
Design Summary results/{build}/m08/{mode}/{region}/summary.json JSON Detailed design metrics, thermodynamics, and alignment stats.

6. Troubleshooting & Limitations

6.1. High-Degeneracy Failures (Exceeding Multiplier)

  • Problem: PrimerLab fails to return candidates, throwing warnings that the degeneracy complexity limit (\(16\)) was exceeded.
  • Cause: This happens in variable zones (such as UTRs or HA loops) where multiple minor variants exist at rates \(>10\%\).
  • Solution: Shift the design target to a conserved coding region (e.g. M1 segment), increase the maf_threshold to \(0.15\) (to ignore rarer variants), or increase the max_multiplier to \(32\) (noting that this may lower overall reaction sensitivity).

References

Koressaar, Triinu, and Maido Remm. 2007. “Enhancements and Modifications of Primer Design Program Primer3.” Bioinformatics 23 (10): 1289–91. https://doi.org/10.1093/bioinformatics/btm091.
Lorenz, Ronny, Stephane Bernhart, Christian Hoener zu Siederdissen, et al. 2011. “ViennaRNA Package 2.0.” Algorithms for Molecular Biology 6 (1): 26. https://doi.org/10.1186/1748-7188-6-26.
Untergasser, Andreas et al. 2012. “Primer3–New Capabilities and Interfaces.” Nucleic Acids Research 40 (15): e115. https://doi.org/10.1093/nar/gks596.
